 ## Search results
Search results did not identify a verified 2024–2026 NextItNet study matching a lightweight title/description encoder trained entirely from scratch. Related work supports semantic–collaborative alignment: [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12183) uses fine-grained semantic codes, cross-attention fusion and masked alignment objectives; [ST2SI (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.171.pdf) highlights limitations of coarse sentence-level representations and aligns item text with IDs. These provide design motivation, not evidence that a randomly initialized text encoder improves NextItNet under the specified budget. Their LLM-based components are unsuitable for direct adoption under the no-pretrained-weights constraint.

A plausible experiment—not an established result—is to retain [NextItNet’s residual dilated-convolution backbone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) and jointly train a small token-embedding encoder with masked mean pooling or a short text CNN. Fuse title/description features with item IDs through a learned residual gate; optionally add a low-weight item-ID/text contrastive loss within the same network. Missing text should produce zero semantic contribution, preserving the ID representation. Compare against an otherwise matched ID-only control; separately ablate titles, descriptions and alignment loss using macro validation HR@10. Token-level features could distinguish names, editions or model numbers, but improvement remains uncertain with sparse supervision. Text similarity alone does not establish product compatibility or unmet need. Keep one jointly trained checkpoint per category and identical feature construction during training and prediction.

---

Evidence supports testing the objective before adding residual gates, but does not establish the bottleneck in Electronics. The [original NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) explicitly supports sampled-softmax training. [Wu et al., TOIS 2024](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) identify sampled softmax’s implicit hard-negative weighting and ranking benefits, while warning that cosine normalization can restrict representation-magnitude learning. [gBCE research, IJCAI 2024](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939) shows that sampled BCE can cause overconfidence and unstable training; its empirical evidence concerns SASRec/BERT4Rec, so transfer to NextItNet remains a hypothesis.

Uniform sampling is a defensible first comparison. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds substantial accuracy/popularity trade-offs across uniform, popularity, in-batch and adaptive samplers. [Hard-negative theory](https://doi.org/10.1145/3543507.3583223) supports controllable hardness rather than universally choosing the hardest candidates. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) documents false-negative risks, although its teacher-based remedy should not be copied under this task’s single-model constraint. The search found no direct NextItNet evidence establishing a moderate-hard curriculum as superior.

Practical hypothesis: keep the ungated NextItNet backbone fixed; compare multi-negative BCE against sampled-softmax cross-entropy using identical uniform candidate sets and negative counts, optionally adding gBCE. Exclude padding, the target and known training-history positives; deduplicate candidates without consulting held-out labels. These safeguards remove known collisions, not all latent false negatives. Only after establishing the uniform baseline, test a uniform warm-up followed by a small fraction of moderately high-scoring candidates from the same model. This curriculum is an experimental proposal, not a demonstrated result; select using the pinned macro validation HR@10.

---

NextItNet’s residual causal dilated convolutions capture dependencies over interaction positions; dilation does not itself encode elapsed time ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163)). Searches found related spatiotemporal dilated-convolution work for POI recommendation, but no clearly established 2024–2026 time-conditioned NextItNet variant matching this proposal. Recent evidence supports investigating intervals: [E-NSDE, NeurIPS 2024](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) models continuous-time preference evolution and interval-dependent uncertainty; [TALE, WSDM 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07382) uses timestamp-based interval weighting and trend-aware normalization; [IntervalLLM, 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23209) distinguishes identical item histories with different interaction gaps. These are supporting mechanisms, not evidence of gains for NextItNet on the specified Amazon benchmark.

A family-preserving experiment, inferred from this literature: condition each causal convolution tap on log-scaled elapsed time between its source and destination events, using a small jointly trained gate initialized near identity. Compare ordinary NextItNet, position-only gates, and elapsed-time gates under identical training and validation settings. Include a flexible gate alongside monotonic learned decay: long gaps can indicate uncertainty or periodic interests, rather than universally obsolete history. Preserve an ungated residual path and use only timestamps observable in each prefix; never use the next target’s timestamp. Distinguish interval sensitivity from concept-drift adaptation—interval modeling alone does not establish the latter. All temporal features should remain internal to the single category network, with matching predictor serialization and final-nonpadding readout."}]
